newsitem.title: BURMA: Top Burma general warns "destructive groups".
newsitem.headline: Top Burma general warns "destructive groups".

text.p: One of Burma's top generals said the military government has been watching "destructive elements" and would take action against them if they did not mend their ways, official media reported on Saturday.

"Crimes committed by the above ground destructive group against the state and the people have been mounting," Lieutenant-General Tin Oo, one of the country's four most powerful generals, was quoted as saying on Friday.
Burma's government regularly refers to opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi and her National League for Democracy (NLD) party as "above ground destructive elements."
"Some people ask why action has not been taken against them," Tin Oo said to a group of military officers.

"The State Law and Order Restoraiton Council (SLORC) has only been watching magnanimously whether they will mend their ways positively. The (SLORC) will prevent any act detrimental to the interests of the state in accordance with the law."

Analysts interpreted the comments as a slight toughening of attitude towards the NLD, which has been under almost constant verbal attack from the government since Suu Kyi was released from six years of house arrest in July, 1995.

On June 26 the SLORC told a news conference some exiled members of the NLD were behind the April 6 parcel bomb attack at the residence of Tin Oo on April 6 in which his 32-year old eldest daughter was killed.

At the June 26 press conference SLORC officials showed some explosives and bombing devices which they said were brought into the country by exiled NLD members to carry out various terrorist activities.
They said the exiled NLD members were acting on orders of Sein Win, the chairman of the self-proclaimed Burmese government in exile.
Tin Oo also said the NLD, which it claims receives support from Western countries like the United States, was trying to disrupt the country and take power.
"It was found that the above ground puppet organisation of the Western bloc has been pmaking preparations for resorting to various means to gain power," he said.

"Some western powers have been resorting to various unfair means in favour of their puppets to gain power. Above ground destructive elements have established contacts with underground insurgents and become involved in subversive acts."

The SLORC regularly refers to the NLD and Suu Kyi as puppets of the West. These sort of verbal attacks have increased since the United States announced in April it was imposing economic sanctions on Burma because of its poor human rights record and its failure to recognise the NLD's 1990 electoral victory.
Tin Oo called on members of the armed forces to prevent all attempts made by the destructive elements to disrupt the stability of the nation.
